name: Annex (Grace Commons Annex)
award: 2024 Federal 9% and state housing tax credits (Round One)
headline: Grace Commons Church is building the Annex, a four-story mixed-use building at 1603 Walnut Street in downtown Boulder with 30 studio and one-bedroom apartments for households at 30% to 70% AMI over a ground-floor café and workforce-training space and a rooftop event center, funded in part by a 2024 Round One 9% and state credit award.
why_it_matters: It shows a congregation turning its own downtown land into permanently affordable housing by leasing the ground to the tax credit deal for cash-flow rent and pairing the units with a commercial event space and café meant to cross-subsidize the church's mission.

status.label: Under construction since January 2025; topped out 2025-11-20; completion targeted September 2026, not confirmed
status.detail: The church reports that financing closed on 2024-12-31, ground was broken in January 2025, the final steel beam was set on 2025-11-20, and completion was targeted for September 2026 after a three-month opening delay. Element Properties lists the project as under construction with completion expected in Q3 2026. No public record of a certificate of occupancy or lease-up was found as of 2026-10-21.

next_step: Watch for a City of Boulder certificate of occupancy for 1603 Walnut Street and Brothers Property Management opening applications (the church said applications go out about 90 days before opening).

key_numbers.meaning: Income averaging across 30% to 70% AMI; 4 units at 30% AMI.

background.text: The parcel, originally a tire center, was gifted to the church decades ago and later housed youth ministry and clothing distribution. The Annex is phase 2 of the church's Boulder Vision Project, which the church says has had a development agreement with the City of Boulder since January 2022.

This was a repeat application. The church reports CHFA denied its 2023 tax credit application in late May 2023. For 2024 the team switched to income averaging, added a 30% unit and three 40% units, changed general contractor to I-Kota, cut hard costs by about $1.4M and lowered the credit request by almost $200,000.
CHFA awarded $961,773 a year in federal credit, below the $1,160,637 requested on the February 2024 applicant list (where the project appears as Grace Commons Annex).
The ground-floor career-counseling space for 15- to 24-year-olds is to be included in eligible basis as a Section 42 community service facility.

The Phase I report flagged the former tire and auto repair use as a recognized environmental condition; a Phase II found no further evidence. The old building had non-friable asbestos roofing and trace asbestos in drywall.
The market study gave a 30.8% capture rate, above CHFA's 25% threshold, but argued demand was understated; surveyed LIHTC units in the market area were 99% occupied.

Construction slipped from the application's plan (financial close about September 2024, construction start September 2024) to a 2024-12-31 closing and January 2025 start. The church's February 2026 update lists a seven-month Xcel delay, foundation and buried-lift surprises, and a three-month opening delay, and says the job was on budget with contingency remaining.
Demand: the church reported 90 people had expressed interest to Brothers Property Management by February 2026; leasing is first-come among qualified applicants.

open_questions: Whether the building opened in September 2026 as targeted; no certificate of occupancy or lease-up record was found.
Final amounts of City of Boulder and Division of Housing funds, and the lender and equity investor.
Land lease terms and the value of the contributed land.
Recorded CHFA affordability covenant term (the church said it would be permanent) and how the condominium split between housing and commercial space is structured.
Rents and whether any units carry project-based vouchers (the application mentions tenant-based vouchers via TGTHR).
